## What's new

- **Based on rclone v1.75.2**, with its security and bug fixes. See
  the [rclone changelog](https://rclone.org/changelog/#v1-75-2).
- **Resumable uploads.** On a KamPlexFS server which supports them,
  the s3 remote with `provider = KamPlexFS` uploads big files and
  uploads of unknown size, such as `rclone rcat`, as resumable uploads
  instead of multipart uploads. One signed request opens an upload
  session and the data goes over the TUS protocol, one request per
  `chunk_size`. A dropped connection resumes from the bytes the server
  already has instead of sending the file or the part again, which
  helps most with `rclone mount` writing back big files over a flaky
  link. The MD5, and the BLAKE3 when the server computes it, are
  checked as for other uploads.
- **`kamplexfs_resumable` option** (`--s3-kamplexfs-resumable`):
  - `auto`, the default: for uploads of unknown size, and above
    `upload_cutoff` while `upload_concurrency` is 1, which is the
    KamPlexFS default.
  - `always`: for every upload above `upload_cutoff`, with parallel
    part uploads set too.
  - `never`: multipart uploads, as before.

Notes:

- Servers which don't support resumable uploads, or answer that they
  have them turned off, get multipart uploads as before.
- Files above `--multi-thread-cutoff` are uploaded as resumable uploads
  rather than by a multi-thread copy, unless `--multi-thread-streams`
  is set explicitly.
- Conditional, encrypted and object locked uploads are made as
  multipart uploads.
- Each upload holds a `chunk_size` chunk in memory until the server has
  it, so up to `chunk_size` times `--transfers` of memory is used.
- If the answer to the last request is lost, the object is accepted if
  its size and its MD5 and BLAKE3, where the server has them, match
  what was sent. With both hashes off only the size is compared.
- Failed requests are retried from what the server has, with
  `--low-level-retries` counting again each time the server has more.
  If the session expires, the whole file is retried.
- The session URL holds the token which authorises the upload, so
  rclone logs it without its query. `--dump headers` and
  `--dump bodies` still print it, as they print every request.
- Behind a TLS proxy which doesn't send `X-Forwarded-Proto: https`, the
  server returns `http://` session URLs. `-vv` logs the URL, so this
  can be spotted.
